phase1_leaf_result.tested_scope: Self-local deterministic replay of generation-scoped deterministic create-once effect outputs on independent paths plus an active-generation pointer updated by path-blob CAS/readback. Tested four interleavings only: normal takeover rejection, late stale output creation after takeover, ABA/reused-generation pointer return, and consumer read-before-takeover then accept-after-takeover without an atomic acceptance-time pointer guard. No live claim mutation, public-source read, external coordinator, or forbidden semantic input was used.
observations: With active pointer g7, B successfully CAS-updates the pointer to g8, and A then creates a previously absent g7 output on its independent create-once path, the stale output can still exist durably because pointer CAS does not fence creation on the independent path.

If consumers determine acceptance from the current pointer at acceptance time and generations are never reused, a g7 output observed after the pointer is g8 is rejected; this prevents stale effect acceptance even though it does not prevent stale output creation.
If the active-generation identifier can ABA back from g7 to g8 to g7, an old or late g7 output can again satisfy a generation-equality acceptance check, so generation equality alone is not ABA-safe.

If a consumer reads pointer g7 before B's takeover and later accepts g7 output after the pointer moved to g8 without rechecking or atomically binding acceptance to the pointer epoch/blob, stale acceptance remains possible despite monotonic generations.
phase1_leaf_result.inference: Generation-scoped create-once outputs plus an active-generation CAS pointer can prevent stale effect acceptance, but only under stronger conditions than the basic pattern: generation/epoch identifiers must be globally non-reusable for the claim lineage, and effect acceptance must validate the current pointer epoch at acceptance/commit time or use an equivalent atomic fence. The pattern does not itself prevent stale output creation. Path-blob CAS/readback linearizes pointer updates but does not atomically couple independent output creation or a prior consumer read to that pointer.
phase1_leaf_result.unresolved_child: Test a zero-cost repository-native acceptance protocol that binds each effect to a non-reusable claim epoch and current pointer blob at acceptance time, comparing (a) consumer re-read plus reject, (b) single-path acceptance CAS, and (c) append-only output plus accepted-effects pointer, while preserving create-once idempotency and avoiding hosted coordination.
